source_text:
Ad Xystum episcopum Romae
EPISTOLA LIII. CYRILLI AD SANCTUM XYSTUM PAPAM.
Κυρίλλου ἐκ τῆς πρὸςἸούστον [ξορρ. Ξύστον] ἐπίσκοπονῬώμης
ἐπιστολῆς.
Ἐγὼ γὰρ οὔτε ἐλέγχομαι πεφρονηκὼς ἕτερόν τι πώποτε παρὰ τὸ δοκοῦν τῇ
ἀληθείᾳ, οὔτε παθητὴν εἴρηκά ποτε τὴν θείαν τοῦ Λόγου φύσιν. Καὶ μετὰ βραχύ·
Οἶδα δὲ καὶ ἀπαθῆ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ φύσιν καὶ 77.288 ἄτρεπτον καὶ ἀναλλοίωτον, κὰν τῇ
τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος φύσει, καὶ ἕνα ἐν ἀμφοῖν καὶ ἐξ ἀμφοῖν τὸν Χριστόν.
thought_title: Cyril's confession of the Word's nature
orientation: Cyril, bishop of Alexandria, is writing to Xystus, bishop of Rome, and begins with a first-person declaration of his own beliefs.
pass_a_gloss: For I am not convicted of ever having thought anything other than what seems right to the truth, nor have I ever said the nature of the Word, which is divine to be capable of suffering. And after a little: But I know the nature of God to be incapable of suffering and unchangeable and invariable, even in the nature of humanity, and one Christ in both and from both.

choices.why: Glossary English for παθητήν; avoids the banned 'passible' and 'subject to suffering'.
Glossary English for ἀπαθῆ; avoids the banned 'impassible' and 'beyond suffering'.
Glossary English for ἄτρεπτον; avoids the banned 'immutable' and 'unchanging'.
Glossary English for ἀναλλοίωτον; avoids the banned 'unalterable' and 'unchanging'.
Glossary English for φύσιν; avoids the banned 'being' and 'essence'.
Glossary English for Λόγου; avoids the banned 'Logos' and 'divine Word'.

pass_b_english: I have never been convicted of thinking anything contrary to what the truth approves, nor have I ever said that the divine nature of the Word is capable of suffering. And a little later: I know that the nature of God is incapable of suffering, unchangeable, and invariable, even in the nature of humanity, and that there is one Christ in both natures and from both natures.

last_rejected.why: The Greek 'Καὶ μετὰ βραχύ' is a scribal/editorial marker, not Cyril's own words. The English renders it as direct speech 'And a little later:' making it appear as Cyril's words, blurring the voice boundary.
last_rejected.fix: A little later in the same letter:
last_rejected.ruling: Καὶ μετὰ βραχύ is standard excerpt formula; 'And a little later' correctly signals transition. No meaning change or reader misleading.

problems.quote: And a little later: I know that the nature of God
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if Cyril quotes himself or another source; 'a little later' lacks antecedent.
problems.fix: Identify source: Cyril quoting his own earlier writing.

problems.quote: the divine nature of the Word
problems.why: Reader may not recognize 'nature of God' = 'divine nature'; 'nature of humanity' = human nature.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'divine nature'/'human nature' or gloss equivalence.

variants.text: the divine nature of the Word

edits.old: And a little later: I know that the nature of God
edits.new: And a little later, I say: I know that the nature of God

fixed: The English already says 'the nature of God' and 'the nature of humanity', which correspond to the source's 'τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ φύσιν' and 'τῇ τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος φύσει'; the glossary concern is addressed in the gloss_edits.
